items.title: feat(pm): add Cost Explorer comparison overlays

Refs #1400 (one remaining UI slice; does not close the umbrella issue). items.title: feat(pm): Cost Explorer — ChatGPT-site parity (CAI perspective, Pareto tables, recommendations, bands, projection)
items.body:
## What this is

The Cost Explorer (`/aa`, PR #1364) grows everything useful from the two ChatGPT explorers — **Site 1** (`aa-task-cost-explorer`, "Model tradeoffs": Recommendations, Explore charts, Band comparisons, Pareto frontiers, Data & methods over AA + the Coding Agent Index) and **Site 2** (`drew-coding-model-explorer`: the task-assumptions projection) — under Drew's rule that nothing from the Aster/ChatGPT versions gets lost. Remainder items are filed as **#1400**, each with its blocker.

Data layer first (one commit was already on this branch): the collector additively emits `cai` (Coding Agent Index rows — score, published task cost, agent wall time, tokens/task, harness, component scores) and `prices` (the #1248 event log's `v_current_prices`); `src/aa.ts` builds CAI explorer points in the `AaPoint` shape and joins prices onto catalog entries as rate bands; a follow-up commit carries each band's rate window (flat / peak / offpeak).

### The five priorities

1. **Coding agents perspective + Pareto frontier tables.** The AA Explorer gains Site 1's two perspectives: *Intelligence & decode* (AA points as before) and *Coding agents* (the CAI point set — its own score/cost/wall-time, frontier flags and beaten-by computed inside the CAI population; the indexes are never converted). Charts, multiples, filters, tables and the detail card (which grows harness / tokens-per-task / component scores) all follow the active set. A server-rendered CAI observations table joins the data section. Below the configurations table, the **Pareto frontier tables** render per perspective: score-first and speed-first over the same score–speed frontier, the price-first three-way frontier behind a percentile cutoff selector (50 / 60 / 75 / none), and price–speed trade-offs — every metric cell with its percentile rank.
2. **Recommendations engine.** Non-overlapping score bands from the visible population (band count 2–8), near-top score allowance, absolute $/s limits, relative price/speed ceilings against the cheapest/fastest near-top models, ranking by (relative time)^w × (relative price)^(1−w), lab-diversity modes (one per lab / labs first / none) and dominance modes (within lab / across all / none), presets (Fast near-top, Balanced, More lab diversity, Tight budget, Reset), per-band price × speed scatter, best-fit / alternative cards with tradeoff multiples and vs-band-best deltas, the "Why these choices?" decision table with per-model reasons, and shortlist CSV export.
3. **Band comparisons.** All six groups — smartest per cost band, cheapest per score band, fastest per score band, smartest per speed band, fastest per cost band, cheapest per speed-percentile target — as tables with scalable near-leader windows (score ±2, time within 10%, price within 25% at 1×; 0.5×–3×) and observed-range endpoint naming. (Lane charts → #1400.)
4. **Task-assumptions projection** (Site 2) in the Model Explorer: turns × input/answer/thinking tokens, cache-read share, writes % of uncached, tool overhead, DeepSeek peak/off-peak window; presets (Small patch / Feature / Repo task); projected $/task, time/task and AA score per projected $ as ~-marked columns, plus a projected-task restatement in the detail card. Priced **only** from the recorded event-log rates — a missing required rate shows —, never a guess. Cache-storage hours are not modelled (no storage rate in the log) and the panel says so.
5. **Inequality filters + saved setups + downloads.** Metric × operator × value conditions (AND/OR, keep-matching / keep-only-rejected) over score, cost, time, tok/s and the three Pareto-gap metrics (score gap, price premium, speed gap) computed against the current scope's observed frontier. Saved setups capture the full explorer state to localStorage with export/import JSON and a defaults reset. Downloads: joined data JSON and visible-rows CSV (per active tab; catalog CSV carries projections).

## Feature-parity checklist — everything, accounted for

### The Oct-25 artifacts (from PR #1364 — all still shipped, unchanged)

- [x] frontier-charts.html: time × score, cost × score, cost × time scatters · frontier vs beaten coloring · family legend toggles · click detail card · hide + hidden tray · size-by-third-metric · per-chart PNG download · bracket dividers · effort-ladder lines (DeepSeek dotted) · short effort labels
- [x] scatter-widget.html: tasks-completed vs duration · per-task / total toggle · nominal-budget ladder · Go-cap diamonds · hollow = non-AA basis · tooltips · "not plotted" honesty notes
- [x] multiples-widget.html: multiples scatter + selectable baseline (Luna low default) · full multiples table
- [x] AA value report: tasks-per-budget in the detail card · frontier figure → chart 2 · tasks-for-$120 → chart 4 + detail card · scores-only figure incl. no-cost rows → chart 6 · per-tier ladders → configurations table · pool seats/plan per model → Model Explorer · Go caps → tasks in both detail cards · peak/off-peak explainer + time-per-task definition footnotes
- [ ] Estimated-time markers / guest-estimated points — deferred since #1364: the feed carries measurements only; returns with #1248 provenance (same item as Site 1's provisional estimates, below)
- Not ported (unchanged from #1364): the report's editorial prose — every number underneath it is in the explorer

### Site 1 — aa-task-cost-explorer ("Model tradeoffs")

- [x] Two perspectives (Coding agents / Intelligence & decode) driving shared benchmark selectors' defaults → the perspective switcher drives the whole tab; score/cost/speed measures follow each family's published measures
- [x] Recommendations tab → the recommendations section (tuners, presets, per-band scatter + cards, why-these-choices tables, shortlist CSV)
- [x] Band comparisons tab → the six banded groups as tables with scalable near-leader windows
- [x] Pareto frontiers tab → the four frontier tables with percentile ranks, re-rendered per perspective
- [x] Advanced filters: labs/families/efforts/variant selection → the filter bar + legend chips + family select + hidden tray; inequality filters with Pareto-gap metrics → priority 5
- [x] Saved setups (save/load/export/import/reset) → priority 5
- [x] Downloads: joined explorer data → JSON download; full/visible CSV → visible CSV per tab (+ shortlist CSV)
- [x] CAI observations table (Data & methods) → server-rendered, component scores as percents, unpublished costs blank
- [x] Model detail dialog incl. CAI components, tokens/task, frontier note → the shared detail card (beaten-by list is the frontier note's equivalent)
- [ ] Band lane charts, main-scatter smoothed/OLS comparison lines, per-chart view settings (third-metric limits, labels, magnification), unpriced-variant buttons, per-band tuning overrides → **#1400**
- [ ] Provisional-estimate points + toggle → #1400 (blocked on #1248 provenance)
- [ ] Evidence & anecdote cards, AA directory with OpenRouter/OpenCode columns, coverage-check table, design references → #1400 (need feed datasets / the #1248 notes surface)

### Site 2 — drew-coding-model-explorer ("Coding Model Explorer")

- [x] Task-assumptions projection (turns, tokens/turn, cache share, writes, overhead; presets) → priority 4, with measured-vs-projection always distinguished (~ marks + labelling)
- [x] DeepSeek peak/off-peak toggle → the projection's rate-window selector, reading the price log's recorded windows
- [x] Derived per-configuration estimated cost / time / score-per-dollar → the three projected columns
- [x] Comparison table with token-rate context → Model Explorer table + rate bands in the detail card's projection restatement
- [x] Benchmarks kept separate (Terminal-Bench / SciCode / AA there; AA / CAI here) → the perspective rule: never converted, always labelled
- [x] Source-data download → joined JSON download
- [ ] Pricing-route selector for projections (Direct / Console / Go allowance), cache-storage hours, Gemini promo toggle, throughput/latency factors, shortlist side-by-side compare → **#1400**

## Verification

- `bun test` (aggregator): **272 pass, 0 fail**; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. New tests cover `caiFamily`, the CAI frontier computation, price-window carriage, and the rendered sections.
- The inline script is parse-checked, and runtime-smoke-tested against the fixture data in both tabs and both perspectives (all sections produce content; perspective switching there and back is clean). Projection math hand-verified on the fixture Luna rate: 3 turns × (10k uncached @ $0.75 + 10k cache reads @ $0.075 + 6k output @ $4.50) = **~$0.106/task**, time 3 × (93.76s TTFT + 2000/145 tps + 10s) = **~5m 53s**.
- Live-data note: `/api/aa.json` gains `cai`/`prices` additively once a collector run on this code publishes the feed; until then the Coding agents perspective renders its empty state from the same code path (no stale numbers).

## Deliberately not merged

Parent verifies and merges; deployment follows the laptop's `pm-stack-update/aggregator` + `install.sh` path plus one collector run.

items.title: id(currency_poc): remember failed transfer IDs in InMemoryLedger (IdAlreadyFailed)
items.body: Fixes #6150 InMemoryLedger now remembers failed transfer IDs and returns the same TransferError on resubmission, matching TigerBeetle's behavior. When a transfer fails for its own reason (validation/balance errors), its ID is recorded in a new HashMap. Subsequent submissions of that ID return the same error instead of allowing the transfer to post. This fixes the divergence where InMemoryLedger would allow failed transfers to be resubmitted and post after the blocker cleared, while TigerBeetle remembers failed IDs permanently. Change includes: - Added field to struct - Added validation check in to return stored errors - Modified to record failed transfer IDs - Only records failures that are transfer-level errors (not chain-level LinkedEventFailed/LinkedEventChainOpen) Fixes: #6150 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Failed transfer IDs now retain their transfer-level error when retried. Chain-level failures are not stored this way.

items.title: feat(mcpx): structured refusal reason codes for refused calls (#1927)
items.body: ## Summary The unlanded deterministic remainder of #1927 (item 6, per triage task 12002): mcpx refusals now carry a structured, machine-readable reason code alongside the human-readable error. - **Defined once** in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/elicit/refusal.go`: `RefusalCode` with `confirmation_unanswered`, `elicitation_declined`, `elicitation_cancelled`, `confirmation_denied`, `confirmation_unavailable`, and `annotations_unreadable`, plus `RefusalCodeForAnswer` mapping a non-confirming elicitation answer to its code. The empty code means "no refusal" — it is what an allowed call carries. - **Every refusal site sets it**: `ErrNotConfirmed` gains a `Code elicit.RefusalCode` field, populated at all seven construction sites in `daemon/consumer.go` — `confirmDestructive` (annotations unreadable / nobody answered / answer did not confirm) and the write-policy ask path (same three, plus ask-with-no-broker → `confirmation_unavailable`). - **Surfaced for callers**: `callErrorBody` now emits `refusalCode` next to the existing `code: "confirmation_required"`, so the exec/diagnose-facing error body lets a caller branch on *why* a call was refused without parsing prose. ## Tests New tests (acceptance-named cases): - `TestConfirmDestructiveUnansweredCarriesRefusalCode` — destructive confirmation unanswered → `confirmation_unanswered`, also asserted on the error body. - `TestConfirmDestructiveDeclinedCarriesRefusalCode` — elicitation declined → `elicitation_declined`. - `TestConfirmedCallCarriesNoRefusalCode` — a confirmed call proceeds, no refusal. - `TestWritePolicyAskWithNoBrokerCarriesRefusalCode` — `confirmation_unavailable` + body fields. - `elicit` unit tests: codes distinct/non-empty; `RefusalCodeForAnswer` mapping. Laptop runs: `go test ./internal/elicit/... ./internal/diagnose/... ./internal/execsvc/...` pass; full `./internal/daemon/` package passes (46s). ## Scope notes - #1927 stays open: rungs 4–5 and the rung-3 model warning remain blocked on #1925/#1929. No closing keyword. - Cross-repo check: `dezren39/darwin-nix` carries no copy of this Go daemon code (code search: no `ErrNotConfirmed`/`confirmDestructive`), so no mcpx port is owed for this change. Refs #1927 · queue task 12667 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Confirmation and write-policy refusals now include specific reasons, such as unanswered, declined, unavailable, or unreadable requests. * Call errors expose the refusal reason alongside the existing confirmation-required status. * **Tests** * Added coverage for refusal reasons and confirmation outcomes.

items.body:
Implements issue #3762 (D1-040, design in PR #3760): the documents/document session frame pair, modelled on records.

**Frames & serving**
- ClientFrame::Documents { capability, prefix, after } / ClientFrame::Document { capability, name }; ServerFrame::Documents { names, next_after } (deliberately no sequence — the listing is a point-in-time snapshot of the blob-store tag set) / ServerFrame::Document { name, size, text }.
- Serving logic (list_public_documents / read_public_document, name rules, 64 KiB read cap) moves from world_ssh.rs into the session layer (documents_session / document_session beside records_session); list paging uses the records byte-page rule with an exclusive next_after. Authorization is the records rule (join capability to participant, else "join denied"); failures ride send_error with the existing DocumentError strings.
- The store reaches the session via WorldService's blob store, or SessionConfig.documents_store for transports that hold the store directly (the SSH shell, per design decision 7's structural note) — threaded through both the query and joined phases.

**SSH shell becomes a rendering client**
- command_frame gains documents / documents_continue / document arms; the shell drains pages under the old list caps (512 items / 32 KiB of name lines) and renders the listing in the previous byte-identical format; /document renders the "--- {name} ({size} bytes; read-only) ---" header from the frame fields.

**Contract**
- documents / document added to shell-contract.v1.json (client + server) and to the shell_contract frame lists/tests.

**Tests**
- New session tests: listing order/content, prefix, exclusive after, read, parity (frame-served listing == rendered listing for the same store), refusal strings (missing / non-viewable / binary / oversized), join-denied for both frames, joined-phase list+read, and a page-budget unit test.
- Existing tests pass: documents_are_listed_read_and_refused_over_a_session, a_shell_lists_and_views_read_only_documents_from_its_server_store (ssh feature, frame-backed path), document_reader_limits_names_sizes_and_binary_content, records_are_paged_prefixed_and_queryable_while_joined, shell_contract suite (8 tests).

**Not in this PR** (remainder, tracked on the issue): the minimal web documents panel + web contract tests from design decision 8.

Fixes #3762 (core protocol + SSH parity; the web panel remainder is called out on the issue — if reviewers prefer, keep the issue open for that slice).

items.title: feat(aggregator): bulk triage mode for Needs-you — multi-select batch actions (#1277)
items.body: Implements #1277 (queue task 4997): bulk triage mode for the aggregator Needs-you queues. **What changed** - `/attention` queue cards (Needs User + Needs Orchestrator, tier and session cards) carry a "Select for bulk triage" pick when the action surface is up. A card whose own controls are disabled (stale tier source) gets a disabled pick, so it can't be submitted against an unconfirmed item. - A bulk bar on the queues section: author picker, verb (acknowledge / snooze / escalate / delegate — the existing triage verbs only), the verb's payload controls, an optional reason, select-all, a live selected count, and a **review step listing every selected item + the chosen action before anything is submitted**. - New `POST /api/actions/batch`: each item is validated with the existing `validateNewAction` rules (plus the #1291/#1293 published-item checks for triage, section fetched once) and appended as **its own attributed audit entry** — never one opaque batch record — so the batch is recoverable from the entries. Response carries per-item results: failures are reported by ref with their error and append nothing, so failed items remain in Needs-you and a partial batch never silently drops work. Client tokens dedupe per item on repost, exactly like the single-action path. - The single-action path and its semantics are unchanged. **Tests** - Route tests: mixed success/failure batch (valid items recorded individually with distinct ids, invalid snooze/verb reported by ref with errors, failed refs absent from the store), per-item dedupe on repost, malformed envelopes → 400. - Render tests: picks + bulk bar render with identities, absent without. - `bun test test/actions.test.ts` — 19/19 pass. Full aggregator suite: 911 pass; the slice3 failure (`dns + sessions + pages routes serve`) and the `web-push`/`@types/bun` resolution errors are pre-existing on clean main in this worktree (no `node_modules` installed there) — verified by running slice3 with these changes stashed. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added bulk triage to the Needs User and Needs Orchestrator queues. Select eligible cards and acknowledge, snooze, escalate, or delegate them together, with an optional reason. * Review selected actions before submitting. If results are uncertain, retry without changing the reviewed actions; successful actions are cleared, while unsuccessful ones remain selected. Successful batches refresh the page. * Cards with stale sources cannot be selected for bulk actions.

items.title: Phase 4: read-only replica world service and spectators (#806)
items.body:
## Summary

From verified replica journal to offline spectator service:

`DurableReceiver` → non-mutating parse/restore → directory-aware capability authorization → program reconstruction/Records → read-only `WorldHandle` → existing world session protocol.

- Phase 3 PR #4634 is merged at `844fac4c333baaeb5e5871298bedaa4beb095b69`.
- Replica restore preserves journaled presence without synthesizing leave events; only JOIN is effective on replicas.
- The actor refuses local mutations, events, schedules, ticks, program capability effects, and journal writes. Replica opens replay directory and artifact sidecars without repairing them.
- No CLI/configuration or offline admission policy is added; phase 5 task 6699 owns authenticated sidecar refresh and Drew's explicit decision.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no replica open/serve path; the durable receiver only persisted and verified journal bytes.
- **After:** `cargo test --lib replica` — 51 passed; `cargo test --lib read_only_` — 4 passed. Includes friend-delegated authorization with no writer actor, nested-group/old-directory replay, checkpoint refusal, the existing session protocol, mutation refusal, offline module restore and Records parity, and unchanged sidecars. Existing friend-delegation and session-contract tests also pass.
- **CI coverage:** current `id-check.yml` lacks a `pull_request` trigger (tracked in #3045). Manually dispatched on the current head as run [41564760029](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/41564760029); results pending.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** moderate — world restore, session authorization, and the replica-only actor mode. The writer path remains unchanged by default.
